Source: https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/chart.md

# Charts

<!-- preview chart 300 -->

Package `ui/chart` builds charts without a look of their own, as headless
libraries such as visx do on the web, with the parts of Swift Charts:
scales that map data onto a plot and pick round ticks, a plot with axes
around it, marks that are elements you style as any other, paths of lines,
areas and pie slices for `Draw` functions, stacking, and a selection that
the pointer and the keyboard move. Every color, size and font is yours.

```go
import "github.com/egoist/mygo/ui/chart"

t := c.Theme()
x := chart.NewBand(app.months...).Padding(0.3, 0.15)
_, hi := chart.Extent(app.sales...)
y := chart.NewLinear(0, hi).Nice(4)
ticks := y.Ticks(4)
chart.Plot(c, chart.Axes{Left: ticks, Bottom: x.Ticks()}, func(area ui.Element) {
	area.Draw(func(p *ui.Painter, r ui.Rect) {
		for _, tick := range ticks { // grid lines
			p.Line(r.X, chart.Y(r, tick.At), r.X+r.W, chart.Y(r, tick.At), 1, t.Border)
		}
	})
	for i, v := range app.sales {
		chart.Rect(c, x.Band(i), y.Span(0, v)).Radius(4).Background(t.Accent).
			Tooltip(fmt.Sprintf("%s: %.0f", app.months[i], v))
	}
}).Label("Sales by month").Height(200).Gap(6)
```

Positions on a plot are fractions of it, from 0 to 1: along x from its left
edge, and along y from its bottom up, the way values grow. Scales turn data
into fractions; marks place themselves in percentages of the plot, so they
are built without waiting for the layout and follow the plot as it
resizes; `Draw` functions get the plot's box, and `chart.X(r, f)` and
`chart.Y(r, f)` turn fractions into points in it.

## Scales

* `chart.NewLinear(lo, hi)` maps numbers. `Nice(n)` rounds the domain out
  to the round values of about n ticks, and `Ticks(n)` returns them: 1, 2
  or 5 times a power of ten apart, as d3 and Swift Charts pick them, with
  as many decimals as the step needs, or labeled by `Format`. `At(v)` is
  where a value is, `Span(a, b)` the stretch between two, as a bar's from 0
  to its value, and `Invert(f)` the value at a fraction, as under the
  pointer. `Clamp` keeps values outside the domain at its ends;
  `chart.Extent(values...)` returns the smallest and the largest.
* `chart.NewBand(labels...)` gives each label a band, as the bars of a bar
  chart: `Band(i)` is the i-th's stretch, `At(i)` its middle, `Width()`
  their width, and `Index(f)` the band at a fraction. `Padding(inner,
  outer)` leaves room between the bands and around them, in fractions of a
  band's step. Its `Ticks()` are the labels, in the middle of their bands.
* `chart.NewTime(from, to)` maps times. Its ticks fall on round times in
  the times' location, chosen for the span as d3's are: seconds, quarters
  of an hour, midnights, Sundays, the firsts of months or years; and each
  is labeled with what changed since the last round time of the coarser
  unit: "2026", "Mar", "Mar 5", "14:00", ":30".

Ticks are `chart.Tick` values, `At` a fraction, `Value` and `Label`: make
your own for axes a scale does not mark.

## The plot and its axes

`chart.Plot` lays the plot's area out in a grid with an axis on each side
that `chart.Axes` gives ticks to: `Left` and `Right` along the height,
`Top` and `Bottom` along the width. The labels stay in the layout, so the
axes take the room they need, and the area the rest: give the plot a
height, or `Fill` its parent, and a `Gap` (or `GapX` and `GapY`) between
the labels and the area. `Axes.Label` builds each label, centered on its
tick; it is plain text by default. Labels sit in boxes of no width or
height that center them, so keep their text on one line with `NoWrap`:

```go
label := func(side chart.Side, tick chart.Tick) {
	ui.Text(c, tick.Label).NoWrap().FontSize(11).TextColor(t.TextMuted)
}
chart.Plot(c, chart.Axes{Left: y.Ticks(4), Bottom: x.Ticks(), Label: label}, build)
```

The function of `Plot` gets the area, an element to style, with a
background, a border or a `Draw` function painting grid lines and lines,
and to add marks to.

## Marks

Marks are elements in the area, placed in percentages of it: style them,
name them for assistive technology, give them tooltips, and handle their
clicks, as any element.

* `chart.Rect(c, x, y)` covers a stretch along x and up y: a bar, a band of
  a range, a cell of a heat map.
* `chart.Point(c, x, y, w, h)` is w by h DIPs, centered on a point: a dot
  of a scatter plot, the point a selection is on.
* `chart.RuleX(c, x, width)` is a vertical line across the plot, and
  `chart.RuleY(c, y, height)` a horizontal one: a threshold, an average.
* `chart.Anchor(c, x, y, h, v, build)` places what `build` adds at a point,
  of any size: `ui.Center` centers it there, `ui.Start` puts its left (h)
  or top (v) edge there, and `ui.End` its right or bottom edge, so that
  `ui.Center, ui.End` shows a label above a bar.

```go
for i, v := range app.sales {
	bar := chart.Rect(c, x.Band(i), y.Span(0, v)).Background(t.Accent)
	if bar.Clicked() {
		app.month = i
	}
	chart.Anchor(c, x.At(i), y.At(v), ui.Center, ui.End, func() {
		ui.Text(c, fmt.Sprint(v)).NoWrap().FontSize(11).Margin(0, 0, 4, 0)
	})
}
```

A mark with a [`Transition`](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/transitions.md) moves to its new place as the
data changes, as bars growing to new values:

```go
chart.Rect(c, x.Band(i), y.Span(0, v)).Background(t.Accent).
	Transition(ui.ElementTransition{Duration: 300 * time.Millisecond})
```

## Lines and areas

`chart.Line(r, xs, ys, curve)` returns the path of a line through points,
and `chart.Area(r, xs, lo, hi, curve)` the path of the area between two
lines, for a `Draw` function of the area to stroke and fill. `xs` and `ys`
are fractions, as scales return; nil `lo` is the bottom of the plot, and a
NaN breaks the line or the area there, for missing values. The curve joins
the points: `chart.CurveLinear` with straight lines, `chart.CurveMonotone`
smoothly, without going past the values of the points it joins, and
`chart.CurveStepAfter`, `CurveStepBefore` and `CurveStep` in steps.

```go
area.Draw(func(p *ui.Painter, r ui.Rect) {
	p.FillPath(chart.Area(r, xs, nil, ys, chart.CurveMonotone), t.Accent.Alpha(0.15))
	p.StrokePath(chart.Line(r, xs, ys, chart.CurveMonotone), 2, t.Accent)
})
```

### Live data

A line of thousands of samples, redrawn every frame as new ones arrive,
needs fewer points than it has samples: `chart.MinMax` keeps the lowest
and highest sample of each pixel column, in their order, and the ends of
each run, so that the line looks the same and narrow spikes still show.
Its `xs` are fractions that never decrease; a NaN still breaks the line.
It writes into the slices you pass, and `chart.LineInto` into the path you
pass, so that a view keeping them draws without allocating once warm.
Keep the samples themselves for selections and readings.

`Painter.StrokePolyline` strokes points in DIPs with round joins and caps,
as `StrokePath` would, faster for lines that change every frame: on a GPU
it draws each segment as a rounded rectangle, rather than rasterizing the
whole line into a mask on the CPU. Where segments overlap, their
antialiased edges can look a little bolder than `StrokePath`'s.
Translucent lines, and drawing without a GPU, take `StrokePath`'s way,
since overlapping segments would show darker there.

```go
// bx, by and points live in the view's state, reused every frame.
area.Draw(func(p *ui.Painter, r ui.Rect) {
	bx, by = chart.MinMax(bx, by, xs, ys, int(math.Ceil(float64(r.W*p.Scale()))))
	points = points[:0]
	for i, x := range bx {
		points = append(points, [2]float32{chart.X(r, x), chart.Y(r, by[i])})
	}
	p.StrokePolyline(points, 2, t.Accent)
})
```

Ask for frames with `Context.AnimationFrame` and take in the samples that
arrived since the last one, rather than invalidating per sample.
`examples/chart-streaming` scrolls three waveforms of 15,000 samples,
1,000 a second each; `-mode path` and `-mode raw` draw them with
`StrokePath`, to compare.

## Stacks

`chart.Stack(series, how)` piles series up, as stacked bars and areas show
them: `series[s][i]` is the i-th value of the s-th series, and the result's
`[s][i]` the `Segment` it covers in the i-th stack. `chart.StackStandard`
piles values up from 0, and negative values down from it;
`chart.StackNormalized` in shares of the stack's sum, from 0 to 1; and
`chart.StackCenter` around 0, as a streamgraph.

```go
stacked := chart.Stack([][]float64{app.search, app.direct}, chart.StackStandard)
for s, series := range stacked {
	for i, seg := range series {
		chart.Rect(c, x.Band(i), y.Span(seg.Lo, seg.Hi)).Background(colors[s])
	}
}
```

## Pies and donuts

`chart.Pie(values, pad)` divides a circle among values, in their order
from twelve o'clock, with `pad` radians between them, and
`chart.Sector(cx, cy, inner, outer, slice)` returns the path of a slice: a
wedge with `inner` 0, a piece of a donut otherwise. `chart.SliceAt` finds
the slice at a point, as under the pointer, and `chart.Polar` the point at
an angle, where a slice's label goes:

```go
slices := chart.Pie(app.shares, 0.03)
ring := ui.Box(c).Size(160, 160).Label("Users by platform")
hover := -1
if x, y, over := ring.PointerPosition(); over {
	if i, ok := chart.SliceAt(slices, x-80, y-80, 50, 80); ok {
		hover = i
	}
}
ring.Draw(func(p *ui.Painter, r ui.Rect) {
	for i, s := range slices {
		outer := float32(76)
		if i == hover {
			outer = 80
		}
		p.FillPath(chart.Sector(r.X+80, r.Y+80, 50, outer, s), colors[i])
	}
})
```

## Selection

`chart.Select` makes the area choose one of the points at `xs`, in
ascending order, as Swift Charts' `chartXSelection`: the one nearest the
pointer while it is over the area, and none (-1) once it leaves. The area
takes the keyboard focus, as one stop of Tab, and the left and right
arrows, Home and End move the choice while it has it, and Escape clears
it. It reports a new choice. Show the choice with marks:

```go
describe := func(i int) string { return fmt.Sprintf("%s: %.1f °C", hours[i], temps[i]) }
chart.Select(c, area, &app.selected, xs, describe)
if i := app.selected; i >= 0 {
	chart.RuleX(c, xs[i], 1).Background(t.TextMuted)
	chart.Point(c, xs[i], ys[i], 10, 10).Radius(5).Background(t.Accent)
	chart.Anchor(c, xs[i], 1, ui.Center, ui.Start, func() {
		ui.Text(c, describe(i)).NoWrap().Padding(3, 8).Radius(6).Background(t.Surface)
	})
}
```

For the points of a band scale, `xs` are their middles; `chart.Nearest`
finds the point nearest a fraction for selections of your own, and a
band's `Index` the band.

## Accessibility

Name the plot with `Label` and say what it shows with `Description`.
Marks are elements: name each one assistive technology should read, as a
bar's month and value. `Select` tells it about the chosen point: what
`describe` returns is the area's value, which screen readers read out as
the arrows come to a point.

What the package leaves out: logarithmic scales, zooming and panning,
legends (rows of your own, as above) and labels that avoid each other.

---

Source: https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/checkbox.md

# Checkbox

<!-- preview checkbox 220 -->

`ui.Checkbox` creates a check box toggling a `*bool`, with a label: a click
on the box or its label checks it or unchecks it, as does Space while it
has the keyboard focus, and `Changed` reports a click.

```go
ui.Checkbox(c, &app.settings.Sync, "Sync across devices")
if ui.Checkbox(c, &app.showHidden, "Show hidden files").Changed() {
	app.reload()
}
```

The check box changes the value itself, the moment the user clicks: read
it, or ask `Changed` for work that follows.

## Groups

`ui.CheckboxGroup` creates a check box over the check boxes built inside
it, indented below it, as a list of permissions: it is checked when they
all are, mixed when some are, and a click, or Space while it has the focus,
checks them all, or none when they all are. `Changed` reports a click.

```go
ui.CheckboxGroup(c, "Notifications", func() {
	ui.Checkbox(c, &app.mail, "Mail")
	ui.Checkbox(c, &app.calendar, "Calendar")
	ui.Checkbox(c, &app.messages, "Messages")
})
```

## Without a look

`ui.CheckboxBase` is a check box without a look: a row that toggles its
`*bool` when clicked, which you draw from the value: see
[custom widgets](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/custom-widgets.md).

## Accessibility

Assistive technology sees a check box named by its label, checked or not,
which it toggles as a click does. A check box group is a check box, mixed
while some are checked, and a group of the others named by its label.

Source: https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/code-editor.md

# Code editor

<!-- preview code-editor 320 -->

Package `ui/editor` is a code editor and a [diff viewer](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/diff-viewer.md)
for native UI, designed after Zed's: syntax highlighting, several carets
and selections, soft wraps, folding, finding and replacing, completions,
hovers, diagnostics and inlay hints from the app or a language server,
and the commands and keys of code editors. It lays out and paints only the
lines in view, so a file of a million lines scrolls and edits as one of
ten.

```go
import "github.com/egoist/mygo/ui/editor"

// Kept by the app, as its other state.
buf := editor.NewBuffer(source)
buf.SetLanguage(editor.LanguageFor("main.go"))
app.code = &editor.State{Buffer: buf, WrapGuides: []int{100}}

// In the view:
editor.View(c, app.code).Grow(1).FillWidth()
```

A `State` is the editor's state, kept across frames as a text input's
string is: its buffer, its options, and what the editor keeps of its own,
as its selections, folds and scroll position. Its options are fields set
before the editor is built; their zero values are the defaults, those of
Zed. `View` builds the editor of a state, which is a focusable element as
any other: give it a size, and `AutoFocus` to type in it at once.

The [code editor example](https://github.com/egoist/mygo/tree/main/examples/code-editor) edits files of
several languages, with completions of the words of the file, hovers,
diagnostics of TODO comments, the changes in the gutter and their diff.

## Buffers

A `Buffer` is the text an editor edits, with its undo history and its
language. Several editors, and both sides of a diff, can show one buffer:
an edit in one shows in the others, their carets moving with the text
around them, and undo takes back the buffer's last edit, whichever editor
made it.

```go
buf.Edit(editor.Edit{Start: 0, End: 0, Text: "// Generated.\n"})
buf.Transact(func() { // one step of undo
	buf.Edit(editor.Edit{Start: a, End: b, Text: name})
	buf.Edit(editor.Edit{Start: c, End: d, Text: name})
})
if buf.Modified() {
	_, err := buf.WriteTo(file)
	if err == nil {
		buf.MarkSaved()
	}
}
```

Offsets count bytes of UTF-8, and a `Pos` is a line and the bytes into it,
both from 0: `Pos` and `Offset` convert between them, and `Line`, `Slice`
and `String` read the text. `Set` replaces the text as an edit, which undo
takes back, and `Reset` as a new document, without history.

Lines end in `\n`, as in Zed: a text with `\r\n` line endings is kept with
`\n` ones, and `LineEnding` says which it had, which `WriteTo` writes, so
that a file saves as it was; `SetLineEnding` changes it.

The text is a persistent tree of chunks, as Zed's rope: an edit copies a
few kilobytes and a path of the tree, whatever the size of the document,
and each version shares the rest with the one before. Undo keeps versions
rather than copies, and a `Snapshot` is a version that stays as it is
while the buffer changes, which other goroutines read without locks.
Buffers' methods are safe from any goroutine; change them with
`Window.Update` so the window shows the change.

## Editing

The editor edits as Zed does, with the commands bound to the same keys
(Control replaces Command on Linux and Windows, as in Visual Studio Code):

* **Several carets.** Cmd+D selects the next occurrence of the selection,
  or the word at the caret; Cmd+Shift+L all of them; Cmd+Alt+Up and Down
  add a caret on the line above or below; Alt+click adds a caret, and
  Alt+Shift+drag selects a column. Typing, deleting and every command act
  at each caret, and Escape goes back to one. Cmd+U undoes a change of the
  selections.
* **Selections by structure.** Ctrl+Shift+Right selects the word, then
  the string or brackets around it, and on out; Ctrl+Shift+Left goes back.
* **Lines.** Alt+Up and Down move lines, Alt+Shift+Up and Down duplicate
  them, Cmd+Shift+K deletes them, Ctrl+J joins them, Cmd+/ comments them
  out, Cmd+] and Cmd+\[ indent them; Cmd+Enter opens a line below.
* **Typing.** Brackets and quotes close as they are typed, and wrap the
  selection; Enter keeps the indentation, indents after an opening bracket
  and between a pair, and continues line comments; a closing bracket, or
  a word such as `end`, outdents its line as it is typed. Undo takes back
  typing a burst at a time.
* **Folding.** The gutter's markers fold the lines indented under a line,
  up to its closing bracket, or a run of imports, with the blank lines
  between them; Cmd+Alt+\[ and ] fold and unfold, Cmd+K
  Cmd+0 folds everything and Cmd+K Cmd+J unfolds it, Cmd+K Cmd+1 to 9 by
  level.
* **Finding.** Cmd+F opens the find bar, with case, whole words, regular
  expressions and finding in the selection; Cmd+Alt+F replaces. Cmd+G goes
  to the next match, and Ctrl+G to a line.
* **The pointer.** A double click selects a word, a triple click a line,
  and dragging extends by them; dragging near the edges scrolls; Cmd+click
  goes to a definition.

`Run` runs a command, as a menu item or the app's own key does, and
`Bindings` binds keys: Mods and Key, then ThenMods and ThenKey for chords
such as Cmd+K Cmd+0. An app's bindings come before the defaults
(`DefaultBindings`), and a binding to `NoCommand` takes a key away from
the editor, for the app's own shortcut. `CommandNamed` finds a command by
the name keymaps give it, as "selectNext".

```go
app.code.Bindings = []editor.Binding{
	{Mods: ui.Cmd, Key: ui.KeyP, Command: editor.NoCommand}, // the app's
	{Mods: ui.Cmd | ui.Shift, Key: ui.KeyD, Command: editor.DuplicateSelection},
}
if ui.Button(c, "Format").Clicked() {
	app.code.Run(editor.SortLines)
}
```

`Selections`, `SetSelections`, `Select`, `Cursor` and `CursorPos` read
and set the carets and selections, `Insert` types at each of them, `GoTo`
moves the caret to a position and `ScrollTo` shows a line. `Find` opens
the find bar on a query and `FindMatches` counts its matches; `Fold`,
`Unfold` and `Folded` fold lines, and `FoldImports` the first run of
imports, as an editor can on opening a file; `Focused` reports whether the editor has
the keyboard focus, and `VisibleLines` the first and last lines the last
frame showed, as a half page of Vim's moves by. `ScrollY` and
`SetScrollY` read and set how far the lines are scrolled, in DIPs, and
`LineTop` where a line starts, below the first: editors side by side
scroll together with them, and an app draws what joins their lines, as
the bands between the panes of a merge.

`OnInput` sees each input event before the editor does: keys, the text
typed, edit commands and the pointer. Returning true takes the event, and
the editor leaves it; the others go on as without it. An app's own mode of
editing, as Vim's normal mode, takes keys this way while the editor still
shows and moves the carets. Letters typed at the carets come as
`InputText`: on some systems their keys come first as `InputKeyDown` too,
and taking a key doesn't take its text, so a mode reads letters from
`InputText`. What an input method composes, commits or replaces, as the
accents of macOS's press and hold replace the letter before the caret,
goes to the editor alone. The key after the first of a chord of
`Bindings`, as Cmd+K Cmd+0, is the chord's, as VS Code resolves chords
before an extension's keys.

`NoInputMethod` turns the system's input methods off while the editor has
the keyboard, as Neovide does in Vim's normal mode: keys type the
characters of the keyboard's layout, which come to `OnInput` as
`InputText`, and nothing is composed, so j is j with a Chinese input
method on. Set it in the modes that read letters as commands and clear it
in insert mode. Browsers cannot turn input methods off: there they compose
in the text still.

```go
app.code.CursorShape = editor.CursorBlock // normal mode
app.code.NoInputMethod = true
app.code.OnInput = func(ev ui.InputEvent) bool {
	if ev.Kind == ui.InputText {
		return app.vim.normalKeys(ev.Text) // j, k, dd, …
	}
	return false
}
```

## Options

* `SoftWrap` wraps lines at the editor's width, or at `WrapColumn` columns
  when narrower; wrapped rows keep the line's indentation.
* `LineNumbers` shows the gutter's numbers, absolute, relative to the
  caret's line, or not at all; `GutterMarks` put dots of a color by lines,
  as breakpoints, and `OnGutterClick` reports clicks on numbers.
* `LineBackgrounds` fill lines, from `First` to `Last`, with a color under
  the text and the selections, as the statement a key would run; the
  gutter keeps its own, and lines a fold hides take no room to fill. They
  keep their line numbers as the text is edited, unlike diagnostics and
  inlays, which move with it: compute them again when the buffer's
  `Version` changes.
* `TextBackgrounds` fill ranges of the text, bytes `Start` to `End`, with
  a color under the text and the selections and over line backgrounds, as
  the words a merge changed within its lines. They follow the editor's
  layout: the rows a line wraps into, tabs, wide characters and scrolling
  sideways; lines a fold hides show none. As line backgrounds, they stay
  where they are as the text is edited, cut to its end until computed
  again when the buffer's `Version` changes.
* `TabSize` and `Indent` set indentation: tabs or spaces, as the
  language's files usually have them when zero (Go's tabs).
* `Whitespace` shows spaces and tabs as dots and arrows: within selections
  by default, everywhere, at the ends of lines, or nowhere.
* `WrapGuides` draws guides at columns, as 80 and 100; `NoIndentGuides`
  hides those of indentation.
* `ReadOnly` lets the text be selected and copied, not edited.
* `FitContent` makes the editor as high as its lines, rather than
  scrolling them, to show code in a scroll view or a list.
* `Font` and `LineHeight` set the text: the system's monospaced font of
  13 DIPs, 1.5 times as high, by default.
* `NoAutoClose`, `NoFolding`, `NoActiveLine` and `NoScrollPastEnd` turn
  those behaviors off. `Placeholder` shows while the buffer is empty.
* `CursorShape` paints carets as bars (`CursorBar`), as blocks over the
  character after them (`CursorBlock`), as Vim's normal mode does,
  translucent so that the character shows and outlined while the editor
  hasn't the keyboard, or as underlines (`CursorUnderline`), as its
  pending operators do.
* `DiffBase` is the text the buffer's changes show against in the gutter,
  as the file in Git: bars mark the lines added and changed, and a mark
  where lines were deleted. Cmd+F8 goes to the next change, and Cmd+Alt+Z
  reverts the one at the caret.
* `ContextMenu` adds items to the editor's context menu, after its own.

## Languages and highlighting

`LanguageFor` finds a file's language by its name, and `LanguageNamed` by
its own; `Languages` lists them. The editor knows Go, JavaScript,
TypeScript, JSON, Python, Rust, C, C++, Java, Kotlin, Scala, Swift, Dart,
C#, shell scripts, YAML, TOML, SQL, R, Ruby, Lua, PHP, CSS, HTML, XML,
Markdown, diffs, Dockerfiles, Makefiles, Protocol Buffers, GraphQL and Zig.
A `Language` says how to highlight, comment, match brackets and indent its
text, and with `Imports`, a pattern of a line that imports (`^import\b` for
Go), which lines fold as a run: build one for another language, or copy
one and change it.

A language highlights its text with a `Tokenizer` by default: a function
from a line, and the state the line before it ended in, to the line's
tokens and the state it ends in, as TextMate grammars and Monaco's
tokenizers work. The editor tokenizes the lines it shows, and after an
edit only the lines below it until one starts in the state it started in
before, a frame's time budget at a time.

```go
// Lines starting with # are comments.
lang := &editor.Language{
	Name:        "Notes",
	Extensions:  []string{".notes"},
	LineComment: "#",
	Tokenizer: editor.TokenizerFunc(func(line string, state uint64, tokens []editor.Token) ([]editor.Token, uint64) {
		kind := editor.TokenText
		if strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), "#") {
			kind = editor.TokenComment
		}
		return append(tokens, editor.Token{End: len(line), Kind: kind}), 0
	}),
}
```

A token is a run of a line of one `TokenKind`, which the theme colors:
keywords, types, functions, strings, comments and the others.

### Highlighters

A language can instead bring a highlighter of its own, as one of a parser
such as tree-sitter: `Language.Highlighter` makes the `Highlighter` of each
buffer of the language, and the editor uses it in place of the tokenizer.
The tokenizer itself is one (`NewTokenHighlighter`), so a highlighter
plugs in without the editor changing.

```go
type Highlighter interface {
	// Edit follows an edit of the text, old and new its text before and
	// after, and changes what it replaced, in order.
	Edit(old, new editor.Snapshot, changes []editor.Change)
	// Highlight works toward the tokens of the lines up to last, for at
	// most budget, and reports whether they are ready.
	Highlight(last int, budget time.Duration) bool
	// Tokens appends the tokens of line i to dst, and reports whether
	// they are final rather than a guess made before Highlight is done.
	Tokens(i int, text string, dst []editor.Token) ([]editor.Token, bool)
}
```

The editor calls these methods on the main thread: `Edit` as the buffer
changes, `Highlight` before it paints, with the lines it shows, and again
in later frames while it reports false, and `Tokens` for each line it
paints. A `Change` gives the ranges an edit replaced in the old text and
the new, what an incremental parser takes to edit its tree. A parser can
work in the background instead: snapshots are safe to read from any
goroutine, `Chunks` reads them a piece at a time, and the `invalidate`
function the highlighter was made with draws the editors showing the
buffer again once a parse is done.

A highlighter that knows the structure of the text can tell the editor
more, by implementing any of these interfaces too:

* `SyntaxSelector`: `Enclosing` returns the smallest node holding more
  than a range, which Select Larger selects, rather than the word, string
  or brackets around it.
* `Folder`: `FoldEnd` returns the last line folding a line hides, rather
  than what indentation and brackets say.
* `BracketMatcher`: `EnclosingBrackets` returns the innermost pair around
  a range, which the editor highlights and moves between, as `do` and
  `end`.
* `Indenter`: `IndentAfter` returns how many levels more a line Enter
  opens is indented.

## Completions, hovers and diagnostics

The editor shows what the app or a language server knows of the code; the
app answers its requests, at once or later from another goroutine through
`Window.Update`:

```go
app.code.OnCompletion = func(r editor.CompletionRequest) {
	go func() {
		items := app.lsp.Complete(r.Offset) // a language server's
		app.win.Update(func() { app.code.ShowCompletions(r.Offset-len(r.Prefix), items) })
	}()
}
app.code.OnHover = func(r editor.HoverRequest) {
	if doc, start, end, ok := app.lsp.Hover(r.Offset); ok {
		app.code.ShowHover(start, end, doc, nil)
	}
}
app.code.SetDiagnostics(buf.Version(), app.lsp.Diagnostics())
```

* `OnCompletion` asks for completions as a word is typed, or Ctrl+Space
  pressed. `ShowCompletions` lists them below the caret, filtered and
  ranked as typing goes on by the word typed, with their kinds, details
  and documentation; Enter or Tab inserts the one chosen.
* `OnHover` asks what to show as the pointer rests on the text, or for
  Cmd+K Cmd+I at the caret. `ShowHover` shows text in a popover over the
  range, or what a function builds there. The pointer can go into the
  hover, which stays while it is there, to select and copy its text; the
  hover goes a moment after the pointer leaves the text and the hover,
  and Escape closes it.
* `SetDiagnostics` underlines problems with wavy lines of their severity,
  shows their messages in the hover and marks them on the scroll bar. The
  version is the buffer's the diagnostics are of: the editor moves them
  through the edits made since.
* `SetInlays` shows inlay hints, text in the lines that is not theirs, as
  the types of variables; `SetSuggestion` shows text after the caret as a
  suggestion, which Tab accepts, as an AI's.
* `OnDefinition` is called for Cmd+click and F12 on a word.

## Styling

### Themes

`Theme` colors the editor: its background, text, gutter, selections,
carets, guides, diagnostics, changes and each kind of token. Colors left
zero take those of `DefaultTheme`, which follows the window's theme and
appearance, light or dark.

```go
th := editor.DefaultTheme(c.Theme())
th.Tokens[editor.TokenKeyword] = editor.TokenStyle{Color: ui.RGB(0xc6, 0x78, 0xdd), Bold: true}
app.code.Theme = th
```

### Bars and popups

The find bar, the go to line bar, the completions and the hovers are
parts the app can build itself, as it styles ui's
[bases](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/custom-widgets.md): `RenderFindBar`, `RenderGoToLine`,
`RenderCompletions` and `RenderHover` are each given the element the
editor places (a toolbar over its top right corner, a bar at its top, a
list below the caret, a card above the text hovered), which keeps the
presses from the text under it and the keyboard where the part needs it
(in the editor while the completions show, in the hover as its text is
selected), and a handle to what the part shows and does. Style the element and build its
content; its position can change too. The editor's own looks are
`DefaultFindBar`, `DefaultGoToLine`, `DefaultCompletions` and
`DefaultHover`, which a render function can call and then restyle.

```go
app.code.RenderFindBar = func(c *ui.Context, bar ui.Element, f *editor.FindBar) {
	t := c.Theme()
	bar.Row().Gap(8).Padding(6).Background(t.Surface).Radius(12).Shadow(0, 4, 12, 0, ui.RGBA(0, 0, 0, 0.2))
	bar.Children(func() {
		f.QueryInput(ui.TextInputBase(c, f.Query()).Placeholder("Search").Width(180))
		ui.Toggle(c, f.Regexp(), ".*").KeepFocus()
		ui.Text(c, f.Status()).TextColor(t.TextMuted)
		if ui.Button(c, "Next").KeepFocus().Clicked() {
			f.Next()
		}
	})
}
app.code.RenderHover = func(c *ui.Context, panel ui.Element, h *editor.HoverCard) {
	editor.DefaultHover(c, panel, h) // the editor's look, on another background
	panel.Background(app.hoverColor)
}
```

* `FindBar` binds fields and toggles: `Query` and `Replacement`, and
  `CaseSensitive`, `WholeWord`, `Regexp` and `InSelection`, are pointers,
  and the matches follow them as they change. `QueryInput` and
  `ReplacementInput` give inputs the bar's keys: the query takes the
  focus as the bar opens, Enter and Shift+Enter go through the matches,
  Alt+Enter selects them all, Enter and Cmd+Enter in the replacement
  replace one or all, and Escape closes. `Matches` and `Status` count the
  matches, and `Next`, `Previous`, `SelectAll`, `Replace`, `ReplaceAll`
  and `Close` act; `Replacing` says whether the bar replaces too, as
  Cmd+Alt+F opens it.
* `GoToLineBar` has `Text` for its field, which `Input` gives the bar's
  keys, `Cursor`, `LineCount` and `Target` to tell where it goes, and
  `Go` and `Close`.
* `CompletionMenu` has the `Items` shown, best first, and the one
  `Selected`. `Item(i)` makes the row of an item, selected as the arrows
  move, scrolled into view and inserting the item when clicked; style it
  and give it content. `Font`, `LineHeight` and `Theme` show code as the
  editor does, and a `CompletionKind` has an `Icon` and the `Token` whose
  color tints it.
* `HoverCard` has the `Diagnostics` of the text hovered, the `Text` the
  app gave `ShowHover`, and `Content`, which builds what its function
  builds.

## Accessibility

Assistive technology sees a multi-line text field, named by `Label`, with
the text of the buffer and the newest selection, which it moves; the
completions are a list, and the find bar a toolbar that tells the count
of matches. The editor's menu, its find and go to line bars and their
names are in the window's language
([MyGo's own strings](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/i18n.md#mygos-own-strings)). Input methods compose in the editor as in other text fields,
with their candidate window at the caret.

Source: https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/collapsible.md

# Collapsible

<!-- preview collapsible 220 -->

`ui.Collapsible` creates a disclosure, as SwiftUI's `DisclosureGroup`: a
label beside an arrow, which a click opens and closes, as do Enter and
Space, showing below it what its function builds while a `*bool` is true.
The arrow turns and the content grows into view as it opens. `Changed`
reports a click.

```go
ui.Collapsible(c, "Advanced", &app.advanced, func() {
	ui.Checkbox(c, &app.verbose, "Verbose logging")
	ui.Checkbox(c, &app.experimental, "Experimental features")
})
```

With less motion asked of the desktop, the content shows at once.

For several sections in a box, use an [accordion](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/accordion.md).

## Without a look

`ui.CollapsibleBase` is a collapsible without a look: a `Trigger` that
shows and hides what `Panel` builds, growing and shrinking it with
`Progress`, which goes from 0 closed to 1 open, for a look and a motion of
your own:

```go
p := ui.CollapsibleBase(c, &app.open)
p.Trigger.Gap(6).Children(func() {
	ui.Icon(c, chevron).Rotate(90 * p.Progress())
	ui.Text(c, "Details")
})
p.Panel(func() {
	ui.Text(c, app.details)
})
```

See [custom widgets](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/custom-widgets.md).

## Accessibility

Assistive technology sees a disclosure named by its label, expanded or
collapsed, which it opens and closes as a click does.

# Color picker

<!-- preview color-picker 430 -->

`ui.ColorWell` creates a swatch of a `*ui.Color` that opens a color picker
below it, as AppKit's color well: a click, Enter or Space opens it, and
Escape or a click outside closes it. `Changed` reports a new color.

```go
ui.Field(c, "Tint", func() {
	ui.ColorWell(c, &app.tint)
})
```

`ui.ColorPicker` is the picker itself, to show in a panel of your own, as
AppKit's color panel: a square choosing the saturation, across, and the
brightness, up, of the hue its slider chooses below it, a slider of
opacity, the color in hex, which the user edits, and swatches of common
colors. The arrows move across the square while it has the focus, Up and
Down changing the brightness and Left and Right the saturation.

```go
ui.ColorPicker(c, &app.background)
```

## Accessibility

Assistive technology sees a color well whose value is the color in hex,
named by its `Label` or its [field](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/form.md). In the picker, it sees a
slider of the saturation and brightness, sliders of the hue and the
opacity, a text field named "Hex", and buttons named by the swatches'
colors, in the window's language
([MyGo's own strings](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/i18n.md#mygos-own-strings)).

Source: https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/combobox.md

# Combobox

<!-- preview combobox 280 -->

`ui.Combobox` creates a combobox choosing a `*string` among options: a
field showing the choice, whose text filters the options below it as the
user types, those starting with it first, while a click or Down shows them
all; a click showing them selects the choice, for typing to replace. Up
and Down move among them and Enter chooses, as does a click; Escape closes
them, and the text goes back to the choice when the field loses the focus.
`Changed` reports a new choice.

```go
ui.Combobox(c, &app.font, fonts).Label("Font")
```

The field keeps the keyboard focus while the user types and picks.

For a text that may be anything, with suggestions, use
[autocomplete](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/autocomplete.md); for a short list without typing, a
[select](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/select.md).

## Without a look

`ui.ComboboxBase` is a combobox without a look: an `Input` whose text
filters the `Item`s of a `Popup` below it, which the arrows highlight and
Enter or a click chooses (`Chosen`): see [custom widgets](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/custom-widgets.md).

## Accessibility

Assistive technology sees a combo box named by its `Label`, editable as a
text field, which expands; the option the arrows are on has the focus for
it, and reads as which of how many it is.

Source: https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/context-menu.md

# Context menu

<!-- preview context-menu 180 -->

`ContextMenu` gives an element a menu of the system's, which opens where
the element is right-clicked (Control-clicked on macOS), and below it when
the menu key or Shift+F10 is pressed while it or one inside it has the
focus. The function builds the items when the menu opens, and runs again in
the frame after one was chosen, where its `Chosen` reports it:

```go
row.ContextMenu(func(m *ui.Menu) {
	if m.Item("Rename").Shortcut(0, ui.KeyF2).Chosen() {
		app.renaming = i
	}
	if m.Item("Pinned").Checked(note.pinned).Chosen() {
		note.pinned = !note.pinned
	}
	m.Submenu("Move to", func(m *ui.Menu) {
		for _, f := range app.folders {
			if m.Item(f.name).Chosen() {
				moveTo, moved = f, i
			}
		}
	})
	m.Separator()
	if m.Item("Delete").Disabled(note.locked).Chosen() {
		deleted = i
	}
})
```

The function runs as the element builds, in the loop building the rows:
a choice that takes the row out of the notes, as moving or deleting it,
notes it, for the change once the loop is done (see
[views](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/views.md#events-and-actions)).

## Items

* `Item(label)` adds an item; `Chosen` reports whether it was chosen.
* `Checked(on)` shows a check mark by it, as for a setting that choosing the
  item toggles.
* `Disabled(d)` grays it out: it cannot be chosen.
* `Shortcut(mods, key)` shows a key by it, as the shortcut that does the
  same. It only shows the key: handle it with `Shortcut` on the context or
  an element.
* `Separator()` adds a line between groups of items, and
  `Submenu(label, build)` an item opening a submenu, which `build` fills.

## Which element

The innermost element with a menu gets the click, as a row's button with a
menu of its own inside a row with another. [Text inputs](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/text-input.md)
have the editing commands of their platform's text fields, and selectable
[text](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/text.md) has Copy and Select All. `ContextMenu` on the input, the
text, or the `Selectable` container replaces that menu, and `EditItems`
adds those commands to a menu of one's own, acting on the text that was
clicked, as a chat message's text offers Reply above Copy:

```go
message.Selectable().ContextMenu(func(m *ui.Menu) {
	if m.Item("Reply").Chosen() {
		app.reply(msg)
	}
	m.Separator()
	m.EditItems()
})
```

The same menu opens below a button with `Element.Menu`: see
[menu button](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/menu-button.md). In tests, `tt.RightClick` opens a context
menu, which `tt.Menu` lists and `tt.ChooseMenuItem` chooses from.

---

Source: https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/custom-widgets.md

# Custom widgets

Every widget is built on a base, the same widget without a look: the base
handles the pointer, the keyboard and the focus, and tells assistive
technology what it is, and leaves every color, size and shape to the
elements it returns, which you style as any other. Build a design of your
own on them, as headless component libraries do on the web.

| Base                                       | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ButtonBase`                               | a row that takes the focus, and reports `Clicked` for the pointer, Enter and Space                                                                                                                                                        |
| `CheckboxBase`, `SwitchBase`, `ToggleBase` | a row that toggles a `*bool`                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `RadioBase`                                | a row that selects its value into a `*T`                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `SliderBase`                               | sets a `*float64` from where the pointer is across its content box, inside its padding, or up it (`Vertical`), and with the arrows, Page Up and Down, Home and End, by its `Step`                                                         |
| `TabsBase`                                 | the tab `List`, whose `Tab`s choose a `*int`, with the arrows moving the choice and the focus                                                                                                                                             |
| `SegmentedBase`                            | a `Track` of `Segment`s, a radio group choosing a `*int`                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `CollapsibleBase`                          | a `Trigger` that shows and hides what `Panel` builds, growing and shrinking it with `Progress`, which goes from 0 closed to 1 open                                                                                                        |
| `SelectBase`                               | a `Trigger` opening a `Popup` of `Item`s choosing a `*T`, which the arrows highlight (`Highlighted`) and Enter chooses                                                                                                                    |
| `ComboboxBase`                             | an `Input` whose text filters the `Item`s of a `Popup` below it, which the arrows highlight and Enter or a click chooses (`Chosen`)                                                                                                       |
| `PopoverBase`, `DialogBase`                | a panel beside an anchor, or over a backdrop covering the window, that a press outside or Escape closes                                                                                                                                   |
| `TooltipBase`                              | a tip beside an anchor while the pointer rests on it or the keyboard focus is on it, which a press or Escape hides ([Tooltip](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/tooltip.md#without-a-look))                                                 |
| `ToastViewportBase`, `ToastBase`           | the window's toasts in a viewport of your own, each a status with an `ActionButton` and a `CloseButton`, their time stopping while the pointer or the focus is on them ([Toast](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/toast.md#without-a-look)) |
| `TextInputBase`, `TextAreaBase`            | text inputs without padding, background, border or corners, `ReadOnly` or not                                                                                                                                                             |

Charts have bases of their own: [package `ui/chart`](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/chart.md) has scales,
axes, marks and a selection without a look.

Base constructors return value parts with the same build lifetime as other
elements. Give stateful bases a key with `Context.Key` before construction.

A segmented control on `SegmentedBase`, and a select on `SelectBase`:

```go
t := c.Theme()
view := ui.SegmentedBase(c.Key("period"), &app.view, 3)
view.Track.Padding(3).Radius(999).Background(t.Surface).Children(func() {
	for i, name := range []string{"Day", "Week", "Month"} {
		seg := view.Segment(i).Padding(5, 14).Radius(999)
		if i == app.view {
			seg.Background(t.Background).Shadow(0, 1, 2, 0, ui.RGBA(0, 0, 0, 0.15))
		}
		seg.Children(func() { ui.Text(c, name) })
	}
})

sel := ui.SelectBase(c.Key("size"), &app.size)
sel.Trigger.Gap(6).Padding(6, 10).Radius(8).Border(1, t.Border).Children(func() {
	ui.Text(c, app.size)
	ui.Icon(c, chevron)
})
sel.Popup(func(panel ui.Element) {
	panel.Margin(4, 0, 0, 0).Padding(4).Radius(10).Background(t.Background).Border(1, t.Border)
	for _, size := range sizes {
		item := sel.Item(size).Padding(6, 10).Radius(6)
		if item.Highlighted() {
			item.Background(t.Accent).TextColor(t.AccentText)
		}
		item.Children(func() { ui.Text(c, size) })
	}
})
```

Bases ring the element with the keyboard focus, as every element taking
the focus is; `FocusRing(false)` turns the ring off for a widget that draws
its own, with `Painter.FocusRing` while `FocusVisible`.

## Widgets of your own

For text controls with their own buffer or selection model, use
[`HandleTextInput` and retained text geometry](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/text-input-client.md).

Build your own widgets from elements. An element keeps state of its own
from frame to frame with `ui.Local`:

```go
// Spoiler hides text until clicked.
func Spoiler(c *ui.Context, text string) {
	t := c.Theme()
	box := ui.Box(c).Padding(2, 6).Radius(4).Focusable()
	shown := ui.Local(box, "shown", func() bool { return false })
	if box.Clicked() {
		*shown = !*shown
	}
	if *shown {
		box.Background(t.Surface)
	} else {
		box.Background(t.Text) // the color of the text, hiding it
	}
	box.Children(func() { ui.Text(c, text) })
}
```

A widget whose input changes what it edits reports it with `SetChanged`
on its element, as it builds: `Changed` then returns true for it, as for
the widgets' own. The [rich text editor](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/rich-text-editor.md) does so.

Give a widget a [role](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/accessibility.md#roles), a name and its
[states](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/accessibility.md#states) for assistive technology, take the keys
it needs with `Shortcut` on its element, or every key as it comes with
[`HandleInput`](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/input.md#every-key-as-it-comes), and paint what elements
do not with [`Draw`](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/drawing.md). Overlays of your own, as drawers, hover
cards and menus, are placed with `AttachTo` and close with
`PressedOutside` and `OverlayShortcut`; `Modal` keeps the focus in one:
see [overlays](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/overlays.md#your-own-overlays).

Source: https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/date-input.md

# Date input

<!-- preview date-input 320 -->

`ui.DateInput` creates a field showing a `*time.Time` as the user's
regional formats write a date in numbers, as 1/5/2026 in the United States,
05/01/2026 in the United Kingdom or 2026/1/5 in China, which a
[calendar](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/calendar.md) below it changes. A click, Enter or Space opens the
calendar, where a click chooses a day, as do the arrows and Enter; Page Up
and Page Down, or its buttons, move by months, and Escape closes it.
`Changed` reports a new date, which keeps the time of day and the location
of the value.

```go
ui.Field(c, "Birthday", func() {
	ui.DateInput(c, &app.birthday)
})
```

With a [time input](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/time-input.md) beside it, the two edit one `time.Time`:

```go
ui.Row(c).Gap(8).Children(func() {
	ui.DateInput(c, &app.meeting).Label("Date")
	ui.TimeInput(c, &app.meeting).Label("Time")
})
```

## Accessibility

Assistive technology sees a pop-up button whose value is the date, named by
its `Label` or its [field](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/form.md), and the calendar while it is open.

# Dialog

<!-- preview dialog 260 -->

`ui.Modal` shows a dialog its function builds over the dimmed window while
a `*bool` is true; clicking outside it or pressing Escape sets it to false.

```go
if ui.Button(c, "Rename…").Clicked() {
	app.renaming = true
}
ui.Modal(c, &app.renaming, func() {
	ui.Text(c, "Rename").Bold()
	if ui.TextInput(c, &app.name).AutoFocus().Submitted() {
		app.renaming = false
	}
	ui.Row(c).Gap(8).Justify(ui.End).Children(func() {
		if ui.Button(c, "Cancel").Clicked() {
			app.renaming = false
		}
		if ui.PrimaryButton(c, "Rename").Clicked() {
			app.rename()
			app.renaming = false
		}
	})
})
```

## The keyboard

A dialog keeps the keyboard: it takes the focus as it opens, on its first
element that takes it unless one in it asked for it (`AutoFocus`), Tab goes
round its elements, and the window's shortcuts built outside it wait, as
what is behind it is inert. As it closes, it gives the focus back to the
element that had it, the button that opened it say. See
[overlays](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/overlays.md).

## Keeping it open

`Dismissed` reports the frame Escape or a click outside closed the dialog;
one that must stay open, with changes to save say, sets the `*bool` back to
true then:

```go
if ui.Modal(c, &app.editing, app.editor).Dismissed() && app.unsaved {
	app.editing = true
}
```

To ask about something important, with buttons and no closing by a click
outside, use an [alert dialog](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/alert-dialog.md).

## Without a look

`ui.DialogBase` is a dialog without a look: its function styles the
backdrop covering the window, which centers the panel, and the panel, and
builds the panel's content:

```go
ui.DialogBase(c, &app.open, func(backdrop, panel ui.Element) {
	backdrop.Background(ui.RGBA(0, 0, 0, 0.5))
	panel.Width(360).Padding(24).Radius(16).Background(t.Background)
	ui.Text(c, "Welcome").FontSize(20).Bold()
})
```

See [custom widgets](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/custom-widgets.md).

## Accessibility

Assistive technology sees a dialog, and nothing behind it while it shows.

---

Source: https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/diff-viewer.md

# Diff viewer

<!-- preview diff-viewer 340 -->

`editor.DiffView` shows the changes between two texts, as Pierre's diffs
and code review tools do: side by side or one over the other, with the
words changed within lines highlighted, the unchanged lines between
changes collapsed, and the new text editable where it shows. It is a
[code editor](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/code-editor.md) on each side, with the editor's highlighting,
selections and commands, laid out and painted only where in view.

```go
import "github.com/egoist/mygo/ui/editor"

lang := editor.LanguageFor("main.go")
before, after := editor.NewBuffer(original), editor.NewBuffer(edited)
before.SetLanguage(lang)
after.SetLanguage(lang)
app.diff = &editor.DiffState{Old: before, New: after, Editable: true}

// In the view:
editor.DiffView(c, app.diff).Grow(1).FillWidth()
```

A `DiffState` is the viewer's state, kept across frames: the buffers it
compares, its options, and what it keeps of its own, as the lines expanded
and its scroll position. Zero options are the defaults, those of Pierre's
diffs.

The diff follows the buffers: an edit in either shows at once, the viewer
diffing again only the lines around it. `New` can be the buffer of an
editor too, as a file's, so that the diff shows its changes as they are
typed.

## Layout

* `Layout` shows the old text on the left and the new on the right, their
  lines aligned (`DiffSplit`), the two scrolling together; or the new
  text, with the lines deleted above where they were (`DiffUnified`).
* `Inline` highlights what changed within changed lines: words, joining
  those one character apart so that a phrase reads as one change
  (`DiffInlineWordAlt`, the default), each word, from the first word to
  the last, characters, or nothing.
* `Indicators` marks changed lines with bars at the gutter's edge, striped
  for deletions (`DiffBars`), with + and − before them (`DiffClassic`), or
  by their background alone. `NoBackground` leaves out the tints of
  changed lines, and `NoLineNumbers` the numbers.
* `ContextLines` unchanged lines show around each change, 3 by default.
  The others collapse into separators of "N unmodified lines", whose
  buttons show `ExpansionLines` more at a click (100 by default), and all
  of them with Shift; `ExpandUnchanged`, `ExpandAll` and `CollapseAll`
  show or collapse them all.
* `Wrap` wraps long lines, rows of each side keeping their partners
  aligned; `FitContent` makes the viewer as high as its lines, as the
  files of a review in a scroll view.
* `Font`, `LineHeight`, `TabSize` and `Theme` are those of the code
  editor. Changes are tinted with the theme's `Added`, `Deleted` and
  `Modified` colors, mixed with the background in a perceptual color
  space so that they read alike in light and dark.

Lines are compared as git's histogram diff compares them, with Myers' for
what it cannot split, and changes slide to where git's indent heuristic
puts them, so that a function added shows as that function rather than
its last lines and the next one's first. Changed lines are paired with
those most like them for highlighting words, rather than in order.

## Editing and review

With `Editable`, the new side edits as the code editor does: typing,
several carets, undo, finding and every command, the diff following each
keystroke. Cmd+F8 and Shift+Cmd+F8 go to the next and previous changes
(Alt+F5 and Shift+Alt+F5 elsewhere), and `GoToHunk` goes to one.

* `HunkActions` shows Revert and Keep on the change under the pointer, or
  the caret's: Revert puts the old lines back in `New`, Keep makes the new
  lines `Old`'s, as an agent's changes are reviewed one at a time.
  `Revert` and `Accept` do the same from the app; `Hunks` lists the
  changes, and `Stats` counts the lines added and deleted.
* `LineSelection` lets the numbers of lines be clicked, and dragged or
  Shift-clicked, to select lines, which `OnLineSelection` reports and
  `SelectedLines` and `SetSelectedLines` read and set, as a link to lines
  of a review does.
* `OnGutterButton` shows a + on the gutter of the line under the pointer,
  as to comment on it, and is called with the line when it is clicked.
* `Annotations` leave room under lines for what `RenderAnnotation` builds
  there, as the comments of a review, each as high as it asks; the other
  side of a split view leaves the room empty, so that the lines stay
  aligned.

```go
app.diff.HunkActions = true
app.diff.OnGutterButton = func(r editor.DiffLineRange) {
	app.comments = append(app.comments, comment{side: r.Side, line: r.End})
}
app.diff.Annotations = app.diff.Annotations[:0]
for i, cm := range app.comments {
	app.diff.Annotations = append(app.diff.Annotations, editor.DiffAnnotation{Side: cm.side, Line: cm.line, Height: 72, Key: i})
}
app.diff.RenderAnnotation = func(c *ui.Context, a editor.DiffAnnotation) {
	app.commentView(c, a.Key.(int))
}
```

`ActiveSide` is the side that has the keyboard, or had it last: the new
side until the old one of a split view has it. `Cursor` and `CursorPos`
return the offset and the position of its newest caret, as the code
editor's do, and `CurrentHunk` the change the caret is in, with `inside`
true, or else the last before it, -1 before the first, as "2 of 5"
counts them; `GoToHunk` moves that caret, so Next Change can step from
it. `Run` runs a command in its editor as its key would, and `Find` opens
its find bar on a query, as an app's menu items do where the menu takes
the keys first:

```go
if ui.Button(c, "Find").Clicked() {
	app.diff.Run(editor.Find)
}
i, inside := app.diff.CurrentHunk()
n := len(app.diff.Hunks())
label := fmt.Sprintf("%d changes", n) // before the first
if i >= 0 {
	label = fmt.Sprintf("%d of %d", i+1, n)
}
ui.Text(c, label)
if ui.Button(c, "Next change").Clicked() {
	app.diff.GoToHunk(i + 1)
}
if inside && ui.Button(c, "Revert this change").Clicked() {
	app.diff.Revert(i)
}
```

## Styling

`Theme` colors the diff as it does the [code editor](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/code-editor.md#themes),
changed lines included. The parts around the lines are the app's to
build, as Pierre's diffs render them: `RenderSeparator`,
`RenderHunkActions` and `RenderGutterButton` are given the element the
viewer places and what the part shows and does, and the viewer's own
looks are `DefaultSeparator`, `DefaultHunkActions` and
`DefaultGutterButton`, which they can call. `RenderFindBar` and
`RenderGoToLine` build the bars of the sides' editors, as the code
editor's do.

```go
app.diff.RenderSeparator = func(c *ui.Context, sep ui.Element, s *editor.DiffSeparator) {
	sep.Padding(4).Children(func() {
		if s.Lines == 0 { // a patch's hunk
			ui.Text(c, s.Header).Font("monospace")
			return
		}
		if ui.Button(c, fmt.Sprintf("Show %d hidden lines", s.Lines)).Clicked() {
			s.ExpandAll()
		}
	})
}
app.diff.RenderHunkActions = func(c *ui.Context, bar ui.Element, a *editor.DiffHunkActions) {
	bar.Gap(4).Children(func() {
		if ui.Button(c, "Reject").Clicked() {
			a.Revert()
		}
		if ui.PrimaryButton(c, "Accept").Clicked() {
			a.Keep()
		}
	})
}
```

* A `DiffSeparator` spans the viewer, both sides of a split one, less the
  room of the scroll bar's track while the viewer scrolls (none with
  `FitContent`), 32 DIPs high. It collapses `Lines` unchanged lines,
  which `ExpandUp`, `ExpandDown` and `ExpandAll` show, `Step` lines at a
  time; `First` and `Last` mark those before the first change and after
  the last, which expand one way. A patch's hunk has a separator of no
  lines, with its `Header`.
* `DiffHunkActions` sit at the top right of the change under the pointer,
  or the caret's: `Index` and `Hunk` say which, and `Revert` and `Keep`
  act.
* The gutter button is a button on the gutter of the line under the
  pointer, which calls `OnGutterButton` when clicked; its render function
  gives it a look and a label.

## Patches

`editor.ParsePatch` reads the files a unified diff changes, as `git diff`
and `diff -u` print them, with renames, modes and new and deleted files;
`FilePatch.Apply` applies one to the old file's text. `SetPatch` shows a
file's patch without the files, as a pull request's diff arrives: its
hunks' lines, numbered as in the files, each hunk under its header.

```go
files, err := editor.ParsePatch(output) // of git diff
if err != nil {
	return err
}
for _, f := range files {
	d := &editor.DiffState{}
	d.SetPatch(f)
	app.files = append(app.files, d)
}
```

## Accessibility

Assistive technology sees each side as a text field, "Old text" and "New
text", the old one read only, with its text and selection. A separator is
a group named by the lines it collapses, with buttons expanding them up,
down or all; Revert and Keep are buttons, "Revert change" and "Keep
change". These names, and what the viewer writes ("4 unmodified lines"),
are in the window's language
([MyGo's own strings](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/i18n.md#mygos-own-strings)).

Source: https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/drag-and-drop.md

# Drag and drop

<!-- preview drag-and-drop 230 -->

`Drag(value)` makes an element the source of a value dragged within the
window: once the pointer pressing it moves a few DIPs, a translucent copy
of the element follows the pointer, and the press is no click.
`ui.Drop[T](e)` makes `e` take values of type `T`, returning the one
dropped on it, and `ui.DragOver[T](e)` the one over it, for showing it
would take it:

```go
for _, task := range app.todo {
	ui.Row(c).Key(task.ID).Drag(task).Children(func() {
		ui.Text(c, task.Name)
	})
}

done := ui.Column(c).Grow(1).Padding(12).Radius(8).Border(1, t.Border)
if _, over := ui.DragOver[*Task](done); over {
	done.Border(2, t.Accent)
}
if task, ok := ui.Drop[*Task](done); ok {
	task.Done = true
}
```

* **Targets.** The innermost element under the pointer that takes the
  value's type gets it, so a target inside another that takes other types
  does not block it.
* **Controls inside.** A press on a control that only takes clicks, as a
  button, inside an element that drags drags that element once the pointer
  moves, and is no click: a list's rows made of buttons reorder. A press
  that does not move clicks the control. Controls that take the pointer's
  moves, as text inputs and sliders, keep them.
* **Canceling.** Escape gives up a drag.
* **Scrolling.** Scroll containers scroll as a drag nears their top or
  bottom, faster nearer to the edge.
* **Dragging several.** The copy shows how many values a drag holds, beside
  the pointer, as when the rows chosen in a list are dragged together.

`Dragging` reports that an element is dragging its value, to dim it where
it was.

## Reordering

Lists, tables and grid views reorder their rows by dragging with
`ListState.Reorder` and `GridState.Reorder`: the rows chosen move together
when the row dragged is one of them, the list shows where they would go
with a line, and the rows go where the pointer let them go.

```go
app.list.Reorder = func(rows []int, to int) {
	app.items = move(app.items, rows, to) // before row to, len for the end
}
```

See [List](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/list.md#reordering) and [Grid view](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/grid-view.md).

Files dragged from other apps are [dropped files](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/input.md#dropped-files).

## Between windows and applications

`DragData` starts a system drag with explicit representations from package
`transfer`. Files, text, URLs, HTML, PNG and custom serialized formats can
leave the app or come from another app. `DropData` and `DataDragOver` declare
the formats and operations an element accepts:

```go
data := transfer.TextData("Hello from MyGo")
ui.Text(c, "Drag me").Padding(12).DragData(data)

zone := ui.Box(c).Size(260, 140).Border(1, c.Theme().Border)
options := transfer.DropOptions{Formats: []transfer.Format{transfer.Text}}
if _, over := ui.DataDragOver(zone, options); over {
	zone.Border(2, c.Theme().Accent)
}
if drop, ok := ui.DropData(zone, options); ok {
	text, err := drop.Data.Read(transfer.Text)
	if err == nil {
		app.message = string(text)
	}
}
```

The innermost matching enabled target receives the drop once, in the next
frame. At least one advertised format must match, and the source and target
must share an operation. Hover advertises formats without reading bytes.
Accepted representations are copied on drop; the resulting data is safe to
keep and read from a goroutine after the native session ends.

### Representations and lazy providers

An item can offer alternatives to the same content. Custom formats use
MIME names and explicit encodings, such as JSON:

```go
const taskFormat transfer.Format = "application/vnd.example.task+json"
frozen := *task // snapshot the value that all representations describe
data := transfer.New(transfer.NewItem(
	transfer.Bytes(transfer.Text, []byte(frozen.Title)),
	transfer.Lazy(taskFormat, func() ([]byte, error) {
		return json.Marshal(frozen)
	}),
))
row.Drag(task).DragData(data)
```

`Bytes` copies its input. `Lazy` advertises a format and caches its result
or error once per drag session, when requested by a receiver. Providers
run on the main thread and must return promptly. Prepare expensive data on
a goroutine before offering it; a provider must never wait for work needing
the main thread. External applications can request data before release.

Use `DragDataFrom(func() transfer.Data { ... })` to snapshot a changing
selection when the gesture starts. Use `transfer.URLData(url)` and
`transfer.FileData(absolutePaths...)` for URLs and file lists. File paths
are escaped as file URLs; the receiver's `Data.Files()` returns local
paths, while `Data.URLs()` returns URI-list entries. `FileData` transfers
existing paths; it does not create promised files or stream file contents.

`Drag(value)` alone stays within its window. Combining it with `DragData`
also offers its Go value to existing `Drop[T]` and `DragOver[T]` targets in
other windows of the same process. Those typed targets accept copy. A
temporary random session token identifies the value; native representations
contain no Go pointer and the token stops resolving when the source ends.
Other processes use the serialized representations and decode them explicitly.

### Copy, move, completion and cancellation

Sources and destinations default to copy. To allow moves, give both
`Operations: transfer.Copy | transfer.Move`. The modifier-key suggestion
wins when both ends allow it; otherwise copy is preferred, then move.
An incompatible offer is rejected. Option requests copy on macOS and Ctrl
elsewhere; Cmd requests move on macOS and Shift elsewhere.

```go
row.DragData(data, transfer.DragOptions{
	Operations: transfer.Copy | transfer.Move,
	Done: func(result transfer.Result) {
		if result.Err != nil {
			app.report(result.Err)
		} else if result.Operation == transfer.Move {
			app.removeOriginal(task.ID)
		}
	},
})
```

`Done` runs exactly once on the main thread, including cancellation,
native startup failure, source removal and window destruction. Escape
cancels through the system drag tracker. `Window.CancelDataDrag()` cancels
a source owned by that window, from any goroutine. `Window.StartDataDrag`
starts a transfer directly from a current native pointer gesture; UI
elements normally use `DragData` so the movement threshold is applied.

`Result.Operation` is the destination's final effect. `Canceled` means no
drop occurred; `Escaped` tells a drag the user gave up (Escape,
`CancelDataDrag` or the window closing) from one let go over no target, and
`Point` is where the drag ended, in the screen coordinates of
`Screen.CursorScreenPoint`. A tab let go outside every window, for example,
is `Canceled && !Escaped` at `Point`. `Err` reports a native/provider
failure. MyGo never deletes
files. Remove application records only after a successful move, and account
for file managers that move a file themselves. Existing `DroppedFiles` and
`OnFileDrop` listeners keep accepting files with copy semantics.

The default preview is a snapshot of the source's visible element, bounded
to 512 DIPs. Set `DragOptions.Preview` to an `image.Image` and `Hotspot` to
its pointer offset for a custom preview (up to 4096 pixels per dimension).
The image is copied at drag start; one image pixel represents one DIP.

### Native format mapping

| Platform | Native transfer                                                                                              | Representations                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| macOS    | AppKit dragging sessions and pasteboard item providers                                                       | Text/HTML/PNG/file URLs use system UTIs. MIME names map through `UTType`, with a reversible identifier fallback. Item boundaries are preserved.                                             |
| Linux    | GTK 3 drag contexts and asynchronous selections                                                              | MIME targets, UTF8_STRING for text, text/uri-list for URLs and files. Accepted formats are requested after drop.                                                                            |
| Windows  | OLE IDataObject / IDropSource / IDropTarget                                                                  | Unicode text, CF_HDROP, URL, CF_HTML, PNG and registered custom names; delayed rendering and Shell drag images. Streams preserve exact binary lengths; HGLOBAL sources may include padding. |
| Browsers | Files dropped on the canvas, read as they drop (see [browsers](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui/browsers.md)) | Files only, at paths of the backend's that `os` reads. Other drags, and drags out of the window, have no transfer.                                                                          |

GTK and OLE have a single selection/data object: multiple text items are
joined by newlines, URI/file lists by CRLF, and other formats use the first
item offering them. Transfers between windows in the same MyGo process
preserve all items through the core's local registry. Incoming GTK/OLE
representations are limited to 64 MiB each; native providers must supply
memory or stream representations (virtual-file promises are not supported).

See [`examples/drag-drop`](https://github.com/egoist/mygo/tree/main/examples/drag-drop) for two windows exchanging
notes, files, text and URLs, including a lazy JSON representation and move
completion. The transfer model is reusable without native UI; existing
clipboard convenience methods keep their signatures. `Clipboard.Write` and
`Clipboard.Read` exchange this same `transfer.Data`; each clipboard write and
drag gets an independent provider cache. See [Clipboard and drag data](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/data-transfer.md)
for clipboard negotiation, persistence, and provider lifetimes.
